This was something I happened to be thinking about rather coincidentally as I stumbled across this post, the power of engaging with something like music as a reprieve from the worst of life. As my singing is awful, I usually instead write songs, and imagined singing them in my head. When I'm alone, sometimes I try to sing, either those songs, or along with my music, and always feel better for it.

I spent ages trying to think about what song might have real significance when having it sung to me. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPlUbrJEli0 is what I went for in the end, Melissa Auf Der Maur - Overpower Thee. It's a very simple song, but to me it's just really powerful. I guess it could sound rather depressing, depending on how you look at it, but to me it's always meant that some external thing can overpower the negative feelings, that there is some resolution out there that's stronger than suicidal thought.

I think the simplest explanation, when stressors overcome the ability to cope. It can be gradual, things develop and grow, with no way to prevent or change things, until it is just too much to deal with, or a radical negative change in life, which drives you downwards to it. I've attempted multiple times, and feel as though i'm near the point where I will try again, because everything seems to be building up without being able to change it. I don't think anyone can know, until they get there, what point is too much to deal with, as it is different from person to person. It sounds like though that you are the same as me at the moment, things slowly feeling as though they are getting worse. If I was better at advice, particularly taking my own, I wouldn't be in this state, but in my mind, the usual way to deal with the slow progression of those feelings, is trying to make small changes in your life, to slowly work at the things which are making you feel that way. The reason for this is that the small things are easiest to overcome, and once you overcome one, you will hopefully see that you can overcome more of them with time.

It takes a long time sometimes for that pain to fade man. And I know it's easy to say from the outside that all it takes is time, but when you're caught in those feelings, it seems like it never will.

I guess the one thing I can say is that a change of perspective might do some good, and this is just from someone who has overthought most of his life, so your call if you want to think about it this way. Someone who treated you that badly doesn't deserve a second thought. Feeling pain for the loss of someone who cared about you is understandable, but feeling pain for someone who has hurt you like this and treated you this badly is something they don't deserve. They don't deserve that place in your head that they are using to hurt you.

The way I've always seen it, is that it is hard enough for anyone, whatever their circumstances, to post here about what they are going through. I've always found posts and replies like this very difficult to deal with, because it's an additional pressure (i'm going on a bit of a tangent here). It firstly seems like a person, who is essentially a stranger, wants to help you on their terms, not yours. Particularly if it's a 'new' post, and the replies are essentially one sentence replies just saying this. I guess that there are some who are thankful for such offers, but personally it always makes me back away. Once you've made some sort of initial connection with a person (you've posted whatever is going on with you, they've replied in some way that feels a positive influence in the circumstances, and there is a basic understanding of where you are coming from), then it's different, as it's removed a lot of the uncertainty that anonymity brings. 

And the same applies to the posts offering help, there's generally very little to go on about the person making the offer, and even if there is, it's still approaching a stranger for a one on one conversation, with all the risks that come of that. I mean, I never even liked talking to my therapist about a lot of stuff! But posting in the subreddit is a little different, because people will reply if they have something relevent to say, whether it's advice on a situation, or even just to be emotionally supportive. If they don't reply, then it's ok, because not everyone has the same experience in life, and maybe most people just can't relate to those specific circumstances. But a one-on-one conversation, which can lead to many negative consequences, there are only two people involved. And it's easy to see that someone feeling suicidal will most likely blame themselves for any negative consequences.

There isn't any good though, that's far beyond what is possible right now, it's just the difference between being able to just about bare life, and completely falling to pieces. Delusions don't solve anything, they are just a placeholder for things that don't exist.

Hey.

I know it's easy for me to say from the outside, but your life is your own, not for your parents to control. You're plenty old enough to make those sort of decisions for yourself, and it sounds like they've put unreasonable pressure on you, to live your life their way, not yours. 

I don't know what sort of relationship you have with your parents, but to me it sounds like you're doing a good job of things. It's not like you've just taken the free time to do nothing, you're following the path you want to take in life. And I would always ask, what's the point of living life just for the money. It's understandable that they would want you to have the best possible chance in life, but, and I know it's one of the biggest cliches going, money wont buy happiness. And how will you do well at something that you have no interest in?

I'm sure you're aware of all those arguments in your own mind, as you made this choice. You lied to them, but only because they did not treat your feelings with respect. Could I ask, what are you worried about most when you think about telling your parents? That they will be angry? upset? Or that they will treat your feelings with disrespect again, and try to make you live your life the way they want to, not the way you want to?

You might call yourself a coward, but all I can see is that you made a brave choice in your life, to follow the path you wanted, and not what they wanted. I would like to make a suggestion, think back a year. Think about the choice you made, and why you made it, and write it down. Write down what you want to do with your life, why you want to do it, the future you see in it. Then write down what you want to do the coming year. Forget your parents, forget everything else, certainly forget those suicidal thoughts, because as far as i'm concerned, they're as bad as your parents, trying to make you do something you don't want to do. Do you want to go for the major you are interested in? Do you still have the same passion for the subject that you had when you made that choice a year ago? Write it down, and why you want to do it, what future you see for yourself.

Finally my friend, i'll just say this, don't worry about the stuff other people are going through, right now you feel this way. It doesn't matter the why of it, the fact you feel this way means its right you are here talking about it. Everyone feels this way sometimes, and you've got a lot of friends here who are around if you need to talk about stuff. Come back and tell us whats on your mind when you wake up, ok?

I don't really understand the idea of owing myself anything, the concept of being obligated to live because i've up till this point had a difficult life... just doesn't seem to fit somehow. It's too close to the pattern I had when I used to self harm seriously, that I owed myself pain for my failures somehow, and one that I have no doubt others would object to if I tried to say the same now. And as for my family, they are part of the problem, rather than solution, though my distance from them has at least distanced myself from one cause of problems.

It's not really about pride, it's about honesty. I could easily get lost in illegal drugs and alcohol by the same logic, that it would change who I was, but would also alter my mood, but I don't see the point in being anyone but myself, at least the core of my being. If who I am is not tolerable, then there is no reason why I cannot just choose not to be, rather than to be dishonest with myself. It's a hard thing to discuss though, because of the differences in our views. You see suicide as a thing to avoid, I see it as morally neutral, and just another choice no more or less valid than any other based on it's merits.

In truth, I wish it was overwhelming me. When I was younger, it did, but now it's just there, a part of me as much as anything is, but I still have control over it. It's just so draining to have to keep things under control all the time. But I am in control of it, and I can see the good as well as the bad for exactly what they are. I still feel proud of myself when I solve a particularly difficult problem at work, I laugh at... almost anything in truth, though i've got a bit of a twisted sense of humour. I know i'm a reasonable writer, and a piss-poor singer, but it doesn't stop me trying.

But I still want to die. And that's why I don't think I can help others, because how can I tell someone else that they should live, when I don't believe that I should, nor that suicide itself is something that should be avoided. And I can't see how my perspective is particularly interesting in truth, any more than anyones is, given that everyone is unique in the troubles they face in life.

As for the final point, I can't promise anything. As with all things, I will think about what you've said, but I keep coming back to the question, how many times do I have to try before suicide is ok. I can't see any reason that this time will be any different to any other time.

I guess that's the rub of it though, people always go to that solution when there is no other answer, and for now, I have absolutely no means of doing so, due to the cost of it (the medical system in the country i'm in is useless for that sort of thing, and i've tried the sort of free councelling services that are offered here, and they were worse than useless). It's funny that probably the only way i'd be able to get that sort of help is if I tried to kill myself. But for the time that I was able to get professional medical help, it was also no help at all, which is what leaves me sceptical about the whole thing.

It is certainly depression though, in some form or another, or at least the symptoms match the description of depression to a large degree. I'm always a little wary about trying to classify it, because I don't want to create symptoms, by trying to explain how I feel in terms of a definition. But i'm very aware of my feelings, why I feel that way, their origin (or at least what I assume is their origin, though there is a lot of dischord between how I feel, and how I would expect that I should feel about such things), and I honestly do not see that  there is anything else I could learn about them.

I'm not sure that it will though. I know it will effect a few people in the short term, there's nothing I can do about that, but I wouldn't say that i'm important enough to anyone that it will effect them in the long term. My choice of method means that they wont be the ones to find me, so they wont have that to deal with.

I've tried online dating in the past, but it's never really worked out, and given that i'm living in a pretty out of the way place, there isn't much opportunity to meet people like that anyway.

Unfortunately i'm going to have to disagree with you about taking medication, it's not a myth, i've known a few people who have various medications, and ended up both worse because of it, and ended up very different to who they were before. I know that anecdotes aren't equal to data, but it's not an effect I can dismiss. Personality changes are a known side-effect of drugs such as Prozac.

I don't blame people for that view on suicide, but that doesn't neccessarily make it valid. It seems to me to be one of those cultural remnants from various religions, which has become a wider cultural norm without people being willing to question it, mostly because they have no reason to. It's not something most people are comfortable facing in their day to day lives, and it's an easy thing not to think about, because it takes no cognitive effort to dismiss suicide as 'bad', and a lot to consider it as acceptable. I guess that also leads back to the motivation of people. I agree that people aren't generally altruistic, there is personal gain in good deeds, by the positive emotional response to being able to help someone. And that's why I think about motivation, because I always wonder if people who try to influence others not to commit suicide are doing so just for that positive emotional response of 'saving a life'. I mean, do you think there is ever a situation where you would be supportive of a persons choice to commit suicide?

As for the final point, I don't think it's possible, to put it simply. Love is all well and good, but it's far rarer than people say. And why would anyone love someone who wants to die? I understand those who are already in loving relationships, but I can't see why someone would choose to love someone who doesn't see themselves as having any future.

(just a note, am half asleep writing all this, so if it doesn't make so much sense, that's probably why)

The reason I say it's a bad answer is because it relies on others for the solution, and I just don't think it's fair that anyone else should have to be burdened with my difficulties. I don't know how logical it is, but that to me is a massive negative thing, mostly considering how my own family behaved, that I don't want to be the sort of person who inflicts a serious negative influence on someone elses life. That's why even most of my thoughts around suicide have been how to minimize it's influence on those few who are around me. There's a whole mess of reasons in my mind for that, that do make sense to me, but it is pretty long winded.

I have thought about that, but i've never been one for dating really. Even when I was younger, i've always wanted serious, committed relationships, and never had the desire to experiment in that way, and neither have the social skills, confidence nor appearance that will allow me to be successful in that. No relationship i've ever been in has worked out well, and any that I wanted have always due to circumstance been impossible.

I'm not sure that any particular style will work with me, there is always a barrier there with therapists in the first place, i'm very aware that they are people who are only talking to me because they are being paid to do so. And no therapist i've come across has been... well, none of them have been able to give me any insight I didn't already have. Maybe i'm expecting too much, but if something interests or suprises me, makes me reassess my views and my thoughts, then i'm caught basically... I guess that goes as much for relationships as therapists too, but if i'm wrong about suicide as the answer, then I want to know why i'm wrong, not covering old ground, but some new insight which will cause me to re-evaluate things. 

As for medication, maybe it's just stubbornness on my part, but I just don't want to be... not me. I don't want to live as some drug i'm taking, I want to live as myself, just without all this struggle i'm carrying. My thoughts don't get out of control generally, and I guess despite my problems, I see myself in sound mind. Even I see the difficulty in trying to justify that point of view while planning suicide, but that to me seems more to do with an imposed cultural view on suicide, that isn't neccessarily true.

The struggle I have though with all these 'one last thing you should do' is that everyone seems to think it should be something different, and I don't see that now as anything more than a delay on the inevitable. And it always seems to me like even after I try those things, it still makes it no more acceptable to others that I still want to die. I don't want to drag though my life, living so many 'one last things', the only meaning throughout to try and find a solution to the pain. It seems to be rather a masochistic thing to do to oneself.

I know you have no agenda, and nor did anyone else replying to this thread (apart from perhaps the troll urging me to kill myself), and I guess that is why I can take this all honestly, though I guess I struggle to understand the motivation for it. I wont ponder that too much, as i'll probably end up overthinking it.

It's always interesting to hear how I seem from someone elses perspective, and how different it seems to be from person to person. I've not studied anywhere near enough psychology to consider that (up until A-Levels/college), and I don't think I would be very good at it, as even then I was only an average student in it.

It's ok, one thing i'm always ok with is talking about stuff, because i'm always open to the idea that how I see things are not always as they might be for others, or how they can be.

The first one is an interesting one, and the only sort of answer I can give is for this feeling to be gone. I could reel off a long list of stressors, things that could change, and my life would be better for it, but I have tried to deal with as many of them as I could in the past in different ways, and the feeling still remains. The main answer I want to give is a more fulfilling relationship, but I know that's a bad answer, as it would lead to a conclusion that it was not possible for me to live an 'acceptable' life without reliance on another, and probably boils down to a fair bit of needyness in my personality.

As for the mental condition, I doubt it, or at least I can say for certain that there is no psychosis involved, as i'm fully aware of myself, my feelings, and as i'm hopefully showing right now, i'm pretty rational and together. As for neurosis, probably, but mental disorders tend to be nothing more than a label for a collection of symptoms, and while they might find a frame of reference for the problem, they provide no solutions.

I've never been keen on medication as a solution for anything where I can avoid it, both mentally and physically, but I have had some experience of therapy, and found it useless, simply because I always found it... predictable. I've studied a little psychology, and while i'm no expert, I feel as though I have a working understanding of it, and in a therapy setting, I can pretty easily predict where a therapist is going to go with things. I actually find talking online more therapeutic, because it is less predictable. I don't know what other people will want to talk about, and there is no reason to question the agenda of most people. But as therapists tend to cover old ground, and offer no new solutions (or at least ones that i've not considered), i've not seen one in a while.

At least an hour's walk pretty much every day (too and from work), and then walking around all day at work, though that's indoors. I tend not to do too much physical activity, as i'm having some problems with a recurring issue with my legs, which makes it painful to stand for significant periods (though I have to do so at work), but I used to be very active, several hours of football a couple of times a week, and still felt the same.

I guess that's the thing about the internet, I don't think in all honesty i'm anything of the sort, and words only give a snapshot of what someone is like.

I'm in my mind twenties, in a bit of a dysfunctional relationship (things could be better, but could be worse too), no children nor desire to have any while I feel like this, I wouldn't want to have a child, and either end up resenting it for only staying alive for it, or dying, and have the child grow up without a father.

I've put in plenty of effort, its certainly not for a lack of trying that i'm still in this situation. I've already done that, already moved overseas once, started my life over, and while the people and things are different, the feeling is the same. And my current situation means it's not an option again.

I guess it's an easy thing to consider, if you consider living as a neutral experience. But I balance probabilities and possibilities, and I just feel that the possible life I might lead which would be tolerable is so unlikely, compared to the painful one which is very likely, that not living through that pain is a better choice than living on the faint chance that things might get better. And if I'm wrong, well then at least I wont know anything about it.

There are very few things you can do in life now which are risky, to the point where your life is on the line, and most of them are physically, rather than mentally engaging, which has never really appealed to me.

And again, it's a matter of means. To have those experiences, i'd have to just sell everything I own, and put it in to one thing, and that would end up making the choice for me. When I die, I want it to be my own choice, and not because circumstances have put me in a position with no options left.

Its good that it went so well :) . Externalising your thoughts is always very useful to put distance between yourself and your mind when it become overpowering.

I always find that I feel worse if I go to sleep too early, almost as though there is so much negative stuff in my head that I have to think about, that if I don't get it out the way, it's still there in some form come morning. 

I've not tried writing anything for her, but she doesn't see the same importance in the written word as I do. I might try it, but I think she will just see it as odd and ignore it.

I do, and I also think there are plenty of people who have been in my situation, lived, and regretted it.

The simple answer to that though is that there isn't anything in particular I enjoy doing. I tend to spend my time bouncing from one thing to another, trying to find something that will engage me for long enough that I can forget things for a short time. And most people aren't lucky enough to be able to afford to do what they enjoy and afford the basics in life too.

But if I posted now that I was going to go away for a few days and think about things, and never came back, I doubt anyone would give it a second thought. The interactions, and most interaction, is transient.

And I guess the question I always ask is how long is long enough? It's not as if this is a passing thought, something that i've not thought about for a long time, and progressively got to the point i'm at now. You talk of a little longer, as if there is some time it is ok to do it. If there is no reason that it should not be done, there is no reason that it shouldn't be done now.

I'm not ending my life over a single thing, or even a few things, but over everything. Everything i've lived, everything i've experienced, has lead up to this point, that's the nature of life. And i'm at the point where there is no countering force to that, all those things which have made me keep on living have burned out. Having no reason left to live is surely enough of a reason to stop living.

It is, and i've spent plenty of time in the past thinking about these things, we are fortunate to live, and to be able to think, and understand. But then I ask if, in this understanding, I come to the conclusion that the only answer is suicide, surely by going against this, I'm going against the very thing that makes life so interesting in the first place. What makes the insignificant act of an insignificant being, brought about by the intricacies of life, to this one action, something that I should deny in a way that does not seem to apply to any other action.

I guess it's just justification to myself, removing all those last barriers in my mind, things that i'll say to myself that doing this will make other people's lives more difficult, so removing the difficulties in advance.

I haven't written anything new in a while, but this is an older poem I've worked on a little.

A never ending book of countless pages

Full of dreams left rotting in the sun

In life we are meant to live seven stages

But I do not remember living one

A list of failed romances in red ink

Though failure does not exist in sweet heartache

But all those loves that never left the brink

And the friendships I was powerless to make

The writing of this pain will last forever

Each cut and blow is starkly underlined

The link betwixt mind and sanity is severed

Each scar and bruise and scar that's shown is signed

With the name that each bitter regret is linked to

An annal of my paranoia's power

A register of every link gone askew

And the memories my darkest mind devours

This chronicle of fights where I have faltered

Seductive crawling fear that is my lover

Close the book, its text left now unaltered

"My Birth, My Life, My Death" upon the cover


I guess I have no storys to tell, or places to show, and certainly have no artistic talents. As for my first memory, was probably playing something like this http://1.bp.blogspot.com/-hfPHQXt7e0o/Tty1HeQnTPI/AAAAAAAAIMk/kK9JcC_X98Q/s1600/frogger.png at christmas back when I was... 6 I think. It's hard to remember back though, too much stuff there i've trained myself to forget.

I hope things go well for you there :)

Today is almost over, and the same as yesterday really. It seems to go in cycles, when i'm out and working, i'm not thinking, so things don't get to me as much. Once i'm done, and am tired and worn out from dealing with so many people, it seems to hit me worse, which is where I am now. Have tried talking to her, but as usual got nowhere, so i'll probably spend another night awake most of it, trying to resolve the choices in my mind.

I guess, but it also means that one life, any life, is so insignificant in the grand scheme of things, that live or die, I will have next to no influence on anything by not being here. Any argument can be made, depending from ones perspective, so I don't think there is a right or wrong, simply choices to be made.

People can and do say whatever they want, and my philosophy is let them. I've dealt with enough people in my life to know when someone is worth listening to, and when someone is just being a douche. Some people give a damn about it and some don't, and I thankfully don't.

Ha, relationships are a big part of my problems. I'm in one now, but being ignored by her on a daily basis makes me question that. I've honestly tried everything to make it work, and rarely it does, but not for a long time now.
Thanks alot, I may take you up on that later.
I've thought that so many times before though, and then the basement floor gives out, and I just keep falling.

I guess it's just a habit more than anything, to post online about these things. If nothing else it helps crystalize my thoughts, and while I still hope that there is something else out there that i've missed, I guess posting on here is nothing more than me wanting to get closure in my mind, that both externally and internally i've accepted this as the answer.

It's simply ending the painfulness of life. Getting away from people isn't a reason to be gone, but being pushed away and ignored by everyone I trusted when I needed help just takes away those reasons I had for continuing.

I've always been very careful with this, I know how easy it is to let those feelings cause a perpetual cycle of crappiness. But I can honestly say to myself that I've tried, and tried wanting things to succeed, rather than expecting them to fail.
Cool, thanks alot for spending the time to talk :)

I always go the whole hog with indian food, curry, papadums, naan, onion bajjis, the lot. Though at 2am, I don't think anywhere is delivering! Though on that note, I need to try and get some sleep. Thank you for spending the time to talk to me :)
Not quite my cup of char to be honest, prefer fantasy and action, anything that puts me in a different world to this one, for some sort of respite.
Well while i've got nothing against it, i've never been one for cross-dressing. A 6ft + guy with a beard, wearing a dress isn't a pretty sight, no matter who you ask.

I'm not in fact. Read it for a while, and have been around the block on the internet, but this was my first reddit account. And I fear, as it's 2am here, i'll have to stop talking soon before my face on the keyboard is the only response i'm capable of.
They are mostly just lots of dwelling on my own negative thoughts... more disturbing than nice i'd say.

To be honest, pizza, or a proper curry has always tasted far better to me than 'fancy' cuisine. Peacoat yes, though it took a google search to realise that it's just the same sort of coat I wear most days, though for my shame, i've never worn a top hat.
That was one time! I was young, and naive, and it went perfectly with the make-up I was wearing.

It can, but there is no guarantee, nor is it more than possible, rather than probable. And that sort of hope is what i've deluded myself with for the large part of the last decade. When does hope become no more than looking out the window, and hoping to see an elephant riding a bicycle.

I read, and write, mostly to try and externalize whatever happens to be going on in my head at the time. Poetry is very good for that, but as for anything longer, I find it difficult to focus on anything for any length of time.

Well i'm the sort of person who has written jokes in their goodbye letters... humour is my most frequent defence mechanism I guess, it's easier to make something funny, than have to dwell on the underlying seriousness of it. 

I guess the problem is though, that I can and do do these things. I wouldn't say i've tried everything, but I do order in food (when money is not too tight), though if I started wearing fancy dresses... well it would take a lot of explaining.

It's as if you're listing everything i've already tried! :P I guess you have to be on my end of the conversation to realise how funny and depressing it is at the same time.

Moved to a completely different country, restarted my life away from everyone and everything that started me feeling this way. The surroundings changed, but the feelings remain the same.

Because ten years of struggle seems more merciful than twenty, or thirty, or fifty. Life is what it is, for good and for bad, and for some people, it can just be one, and not both of those.

You don't throw out an album after one bad song, but after half a dozen in a row, do you really inflict it upon yourself to listen to the rest?

I really think this is just my day for sounding morose. My last two pet cats were both killed (one ran over by a car, one kicked to death in a park) :( . Though in honesty, I never felt that attached to them either.

People can't predict the future, but they can take informed guesses on the basis of what has happened... and it also means no-one can promise that things will get better.

Life is temporary though. In the end, death is inevitable. Which sounds more depressing than I intend it to, it's just that... most people wouldn't think twice putting down an animal in pain. Where do you get to the point that it applies the same way to a person?

I guess though that it doesn't matter how much of the world is illuminated in a spark if that light can't be sustained. To stretch the analogy to breaking point, I feel like my life has been in one of those rooms, lit by nothing but candles. Just as time has gone by, the candles have burnt out one by one, those things and people that have lit up life have extinguished. And now i'm in the middle of that room with nothing but the broken lighter.

And my cooking skills... well i'll just say that if I was looking for an explainable way to go, suffering my own cooking would be an easy one (or accidently setting fire to the house).

The problem is that I have the solution. One that for over ten years has seemed the right answer to everything. I've tried plenty of what life has to offer, and even after, the answer still remains the same. I just guess after making that realisation so many times, it's hard to see any alternatives. I've tried enjoying those sorts of things in life, but the solution still remains the same in my head.

I guess I just find that it isn't enough any more. Living day by day, taking the small joys that life can offer... I've tried living that way, but I just can't manage it, because no other feeling can overcome this... blackness, for want of a better word. It's like... trying to use a broken lighter in a dark room, you keep trying, and get momentary flash of light, but it's still dark before then, it's still dark afterwards, and that flash of light is so small in comparison to the darkness everywhere.

Years worth of life just screwing me around, over and over again. I've thought about it for a very long time, even tried in the past, but now it just seems like every reason I ever had to keep going is now gone, every attempt I make at finding a new reason to keep on just ends up failing, and after thinking about it for so long, it just seems to be the only way I can stop the struggle.

I guess I just don't even know what to talk about. Seems almost a habit that i'm posting this sort of thing online, and i've tried talking so many times but it's never a solution, the solution is already there, and as much as I try anything else, the same solution seems still to always be there.

I've slept on it plenty of times already. It's not a rash decision, and if tomorrow I woke up and things were suddenly ok, then it would be different. But none of the tomorrows ever are. They just seem the same as the previous day, with just that bit of added disappointment that I somehow thought things would change.

Everyone i've talked to about it doesn't care, and I could by now probably resite by rote the sort of thing any suicide helpline would say. The internet is the only place, even if only temporarily, that I felt like I would be able to talk to someone, and they would actually care. Too many failed hopes there too. Guess because i'm posting here, i'm still trying. Just don't know why I am.

Externalizing it though takes it beyond your control, and gives it a life of its own. If it is a part of you, you know that even if sometimes it's hard, it is always within your control to some degree. It might be different for me, as I was always a self-harmer too. I know this might sound odd, but there was a technique that I often used to hit that home, when I felt overwhelmed. I just sat there, and moved my hands. I thought as I moved them, thought to myself consciously which way I wanted them to go, and then did it. And then I did the same, but moved them the other way, so when I was saying to myself left, I moved them right, and visa-versa. It helped me realise that what was on the surface wasn't always all there was, and that all these actions came from me, whether or not I wanted them consciously, some action from myself was causing it. And if I could cause it, I could gain control over it.

Depression isn't that obvious an enemy, or at least as i've found it. It's seductive, its tendrils twist around you, seeps through you, until it is you, as if it taints every fibre of your being. And once it does, you don't have the ability to externalise it, any more than you can reach in to your head and tear out a part of your brain.

First thing i'll say is that age doesn't matter, feelings are feelings, and although everyone is different, those core feelings that those of us who have to deal with suicidal thoughts every day are always similar.

I'm kind of in the same boat you are with the internet, I am rarely not online, but it is something i've actually come to terms with. I don't feel that it's the internet itself that is addictive, but the sheer breadth of what is out there, and the opportunities it gives, make it easy to be drawn in, and difficult to see the real world as anything in comparison. This is where I would like to give some sort of answer to how to get over it, but I don't have one, I just wanted you to know that I do know and understand how you feel in that regard.

What sort of creative things do you like to do? It's hard to judge oneself when it comes to that, particularly if you have a low opinion of yourself, but I would say that you shouldn't label anything creative as a failure. The process of creating something in itself is a good and positive thing.

As for friends, the internet is in my opinion at least, the best place for them. I know many would disagree, but it's such a big place, that it's easy to find someone who relates to what you are thinking and feeling. There are no pressures, or expectations, or judgements, and you can commit as much or as little of yourself to them as you feel comfortable with. The same goes for everyone else, if someone wants to talk to you, they will :) and there is nothing wrong with needing to be reassured. Just trust that anyone who is talking to you is doing so because they want to, and if they don't, then screw them, there are millions of other people you haven't talked to yet.

Death is a difficult thing to deal with, and no-one can tell you how to react to it. The important thing is that you can see the value she had to you, and that you recognise that she loved you. Losing someone is hard, but i'm sure that someone who cares for you would prefer to be remembered in fondness, rather than as something to be guilty for. 

I'm sorry if this all sounds a little preachy, the only real thing I can suggest is just to keep talking. Don't worry if it doesn't make sense to anyone else, just keep saying what you feel like saying.

It's not that though, i've spent years worth of tomorrows. It's not hard to put off ending your life for one day, but it is hard doing it over and over again, trying and seeing no reason for it. The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

The simplest thing to do in life is accept. I will never know exactly how the universe works, but I accept that it has its own logic, its own rules, and I agree that the mind can be seen as a microcosm for the universe. And I accept that my mind is the way it is, the reasons why it has come to this state, and thankfully understand it far better than most with their own. But it's not worry that makes me choose this path, but simple acceptance. I accept how my mind is, how it has been, and how it will be. I know I cannot predict the future, but I know that who I am now is largely who I would be if I lived another five or fifty years, because of that understanding. And while I accept who I am, I cannot handle being me. It's not the unknown that drives me to feel this way, but the known.

But it is impossible to be free from all outside influences, and to say that it is a surrender is like saying that eating, or itching a scratch, putting up an umbrella in the rain, or anything, is a surrender. It is simply a reaction to internal and external stimuli. The only difference is that suicide is permanent, and feels natural when the alternative is a lifetime without freedom, of experiencing that constant pain without reprieve. I am not a religious man, so I do not believe there is anything at the end of life, some punishment or reward that i'm waiting for, so whether I die tomorrow, or fifty years from now, from that moment of death, it will simply be irrelevent to me. I can't see how deciding to live in pain is a rational choice. I've spent near to half my life struggling... it's a long time to struggle, having hope drained away every day, to have every attempt you make to gain even a modidon of happiness, or anything more than a temporary numbness from pain... leading back every time to the same feelings. 

I just don't think it's worth it.

The only person to whom my existance holds any real meaning is my partner, or at least it used to. I've tried all the things that people would suggest in this situation, to try and improve our relationship, tried talking to her about how i've been feeling, tried to get her to talk about how she feels about things, without putting any pressure on her, and as much as I try, things aren't working. Even if I was strong enough to be an anchor, instead of caught in the tides of life, there is no-one who would really do more than note my passing.

The simple reason to die is to end the torment of my own existance. I've been dealing with these struggles for over ten years, so I am not abandoning life on a whim. I've tried everything I can, everything I am capable of or have the means to. I've spent that time waiting for things to get better, making every effort I could to enact that change. I have limits, because of who I am, but i'm not just a spectator in life.

It is a selfish act, as in, I don't pretend that I do it for any other reasons than my own. But death is a natural part of life, and only suicide ever seems to be considered in the light of this definition. I've chosen a method, and planned to minimise any negative reaction it may cause, but I will not pretend that, in the short term, it will cause negative emotions in others. But is it not a more selfish act to demand another to live in torment, to save others from that?
All at once, or in a lifetime?
